gaps.concept: CRH stimulates pituitary ACTH release; ACTH stimulates zona fasciculata cortisol synthesis; cortisol inhibits CRH and ACTH by negative feedback.
gaps.why_tested: Explains hormone changes after an adrenal lesion, pituitary lesion, or glucocorticoid exposure.

gaps.concept: Glucocorticoids bind intracellular receptors that regulate gene transcription.
gaps.why_tested: A drug mechanism question asks how steroids produce their delayed effects.

gaps.concept: Exogenous glucocorticoid excess causes cushingoid features with low ACTH, low endogenous cortisol, and bilateral adrenal atrophy.
gaps.why_tested: A cushingoid patient taking steroids has unexpectedly low measured cortisol and ACTH.

gaps.concept: ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome causes bilateral adrenal cortical hyperplasia.
gaps.why_tested: Bilateral adrenal enlargement must be distinguished from a cortisol-secreting unilateral adrenal tumor.

gaps.concept: Failure of morning cortisol to suppress after low-dose dexamethasone supports Cushing syndrome.
gaps.why_tested: A stem supplies results of an overnight dexamethasone screening test.

gaps.concept: Pituitary Cushing disease usually increases ACTH after CRH; a central-to-peripheral ACTH gradient on petrosal sampling favors a pituitary source.
gaps.why_tested: Dynamic-test results distinguish a corticotroph adenoma from ectopic ACTH secretion.

gaps.concept: Severe cortisol excess overwhelms renal 11β-HSD2, activating mineralocorticoid receptors and causing hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis with low renin and aldosterone.
gaps.why_tested: Hypertension and hypokalemia occur despite suppressed aldosterone.

gaps.concept: In children, weight gain with slowing linear growth is a characteristic clue to Cushing syndrome.
gaps.why_tested: A child gains weight while crossing downward on the height growth chart.

gaps.concept: Adrenocortical carcinoma may co-secrete androgens, causing rapidly progressive Cushing features with virilization.
gaps.why_tested: Rapid onset and virilization help identify an adrenal carcinoma.

gaps.concept: Alcohol use disorder and major depression can produce reversible, non-neoplastic hypercortisolism resembling Cushing syndrome.
gaps.why_tested: Cushing-like findings accompany a condition that can activate the HPA axis.

gaps.concept: Primary adrenal insufficiency causes high ACTH and high renin alongside low cortisol and aldosterone.
gaps.why_tested: A hormone panel must localize adrenal failure to the adrenal cortex.

gaps.concept: Elevated ACTH-derived melanocyte-stimulating peptides cause Addison hyperpigmentation, especially in skin creases and oral mucosa.
gaps.why_tested: Mucosal pigmentation distinguishes primary from central adrenal insufficiency.

gaps.concept: Aldosterone deficiency in primary adrenal insufficiency causes salt craving, volume depletion, and hyperkalemic non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis.
gaps.why_tested: Salt craving and an acid–base result clarify the source of hypotension.

gaps.concept: Cortisol deficiency increases ADH release, causing dilutional hyponatremia even when aldosterone is preserved in central adrenal insufficiency.
gaps.why_tested: Hyponatremia without hyperkalemia points toward central adrenal insufficiency.

gaps.concept: Autoimmune Addison disease is associated with 21-hydroxylase antibodies and lymphocytic destruction of the adrenal cortex.
gaps.why_tested: An antibody result or adrenal histology identifies the cause of primary insufficiency.

gaps.concept: Adrenal tuberculosis can produce caseating granulomas and bilateral adrenal enlargement or calcification.
gaps.why_tested: Adrenal imaging or pathology distinguishes tuberculosis from autoimmune adrenalitis.

gaps.concept: The cosyntropin test shows little cortisol rise in primary insufficiency; recent central insufficiency may respond before adrenal atrophy develops.
gaps.why_tested: A normal stimulation result after a new pituitary injury does not exclude central insufficiency.

gaps.concept: Pituitary disease or surgery can cause secondary adrenal insufficiency; hypothalamic disease can cause tertiary insufficiency.
gaps.why_tested: A low ACTH–low cortisol pattern follows a sellar lesion or operation.

gaps.concept: Primary adrenal insufficiency requires glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement; central insufficiency generally requires glucocorticoid replacement alone.
gaps.why_tested: A treatment-choice question hinges on whether aldosterone production is preserved.

gaps.concept: Hydrocortisone has glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid activity; dexamethasone is long acting and has negligible mineralocorticoid activity.
gaps.why_tested: Drug properties determine which steroid can replace cortisol or serve in a suppression test.

gaps.concept: Ketoconazole inhibits adrenal steroid-synthesizing CYP enzymes and may cause hepatotoxicity, reduced testosterone, and gynecomastia.
gaps.why_tested: Adverse effects identify the steroidogenesis inhibitor used for hypercortisolism.

gaps.concept: Metyrapone increases androgen and deoxycorticosterone precursors, potentially causing hirsutism, hypertension, and hypokalemia.
gaps.why_tested: New hirsutism or mineralocorticoid effects follow treatment of Cushing syndrome.

gaps.concept: Glucocorticoid-induced neutrophilia results chiefly from neutrophil demargination, despite impaired inflammatory cell migration.
gaps.why_tested: Leukocytosis after steroid administration occurs without evidence of bacterial infection.

gaps.concept: AIRE deficiency impairs thymic negative selection, causing the autoimmune manifestations of APS-1.
gaps.why_tested: An immune-tolerance mechanism explains candidiasis and multiple endocrine failures.

gaps.concept: X-linked ABCD1 transporter deficiency prevents peroxisomal handling of very-long-chain fatty acids in adrenoleukodystrophy.
gaps.why_tested: A boy with adrenal failure and demyelination has a peroxisomal transporter defect.

gaps.concept: Transsphenoidal resection is first-line treatment for a pituitary ACTH-secreting adenoma.
gaps.why_tested: A first-line treatment question presents confirmed Cushing disease.
